A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FuseLIP and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A and B. Content can be matched despite substantial reformatting, renumbering, and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations, hard-negative and loss ablations, runtime measurements, and appendix experiments on compositionality, modality gaps, and fine-tuning.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds original experiments on tokenizer and encoder configurations, comparison models, loss components, and training-seed variability.

M1.justification: The proposed frozen TiTok tokenizer, shared bidirectional transformer, token concatenation, final-token embedding, combined SigLIP/MMM objective, and hard-negative procedure remain unchanged. V2 clarifies their operation; the newly tested configurations are experimental controls rather than revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation retain the same dataset and task coverage, including CC3M/CC12M, generated multimodal tasks, Visual Genome, HQ-Edit, MMEB, OpenImages tasks, ImageNet, and SugarCrepe. V2's unimodal-task table aggregates previously evaluated MMEB subtasks rather than introducing new coverage.

E2.justification: V2 substantially expands the controlled comparisons with TiTok-SigLIP-BMLF and small/base SigLIP-MLF variants using frozen pretrained encoders (Tables 14–15). These examine alternatives absent from v1. Pretrained SigLIP and VLM2Vec are retained comparisons moved from v1 Table 11 to v2 Table 5, not new baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols independently cross tokenizer and transformer sizes at a fixed 128-token budget, supply TiTok tokens to late fusion, pretrain and freeze SigLIP backbones before multimodal training, and train with MMM alone. Main training budgets remain unchanged. V2 also corrects OI-Crop's main-text description from five to four same-image negatives, matching v1 Appendix A.4 rather than establishing an actual dataset change.

E4.justification: Appendix B adds substantial analyses separating tokenizer fidelity from encoder size, testing tokenizer pretraining as an explanation for gains, evaluating frozen backbones, checking the necessity of contrastive loss, and examining unimodal performance separately (Tables 13–17). Existing loss and hard-negative ablations remain. The CC3M-trained per-transformation TGIT breakdown is removed; the CC12M-trained breakdown remains.

E5.justification: V1 reports benchmark point estimates without training-seed uncertainty. V2 Table 10 reports means and standard deviations across three different training seeds for FuseLIP-B and SigLIP-BMLF on CC3M+MM across nine benchmarks. V1's training-run count is unspecified, so an increase from a particular earlier count cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: V2 adds results for the new controls, seed averages, and unimodal aggregates. For example, Table 14 reports 69.3% TGIT for TiTok-SigLIP-BMLF, and Table 16 reports 0.2% VQA for MMM-only FuseLIP-S. Main Table 3 scores remain identical. V2 removes the CC3M per-transformation TGIT scores and corrects OI-Crop random chance from 1.0% to 10.0% in the relocated fine-tuning comparison.

T1.justification: The SigLIP, multimodal SigLIP, MMM, combined-objective, and modality-gap formulations are unchanged. V2 adds explanatory qualifications but no new substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract changes from claiming comparable unimodal performance to claiming outperformance on several unimodal as well as multimodal tasks. The central contributions—early fusion through a single encoder, combined training objectives, and multimodal datasets and evaluations—remain the same.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly limits TGIT findings to learning transformation families represented during training, acknowledges FuseLIP-S's weaker classification/retrieval performance, and qualifies MMM as an additional benefit rather than the sole explanation for gains. Appendix B distinguishes tokenizer fidelity from token-budget scaling and interprets the new controls. Additional discussion addresses inference-cost amortization and specific risks from caption-generated data and spatial-localization capabilities.

D1.justification: V2 clarifies positional embeddings across the concatenated sequence, cosine-similarity retrieval, category-level mean top-1 accuracy, and the 80-template ImageNet evaluation. It explicitly advertises code and dataset release, whereas v1 advertises code and models. Existing training hyperparameters and asset links are retained; the PDFs alone do not verify external resource availability.

R1.justification: Related work adds VisualBERT, UNITER, recurrence-enhanced retrieval, newer multimodal-LLM embedding work, and DALL-E, while explicitly distinguishing embedding research from other early-fusion applications. Some citations, including DreamSim and EVA-CLIP, disappear. These are targeted positioning updates; the central relationship to CLIP, SigLIP, FLAVA, and MagicLens remains.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence and much of the prose remain. V2 edits wording and explanations, folds Setup into Experiments, moves MMEB fine-tuning and external-model comparisons from Appendix B into the main results, relocates Limitations into Discussion, and adds Broader Impact. These are bounded reorganizations within the existing narrative.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a different publication layout, redraws the architecture diagram, condenses Figure 2, and redisplays an existing horizontal-flip example as main-text Figure 3. It adds several analysis tables, introduces zero-shot markers, relocates and compresses the fine-tuning table, reduces Table 4 to CC12M results, and reorders appendix displays. These changes extend well beyond pagination.

improvement.justification: V1's attribution of gains to early fusion left tokenizer quality and pretraining insufficiently separated from architecture. V2's controlled experiments in Tables 13–16 substantially address that gap, while Table 10 adds evidence about training stability. Clearer TGIT applicability boundaries also improve interpretation. The lost CC3M transformation breakdown and small unexplained cross-table discrepancies, such as FuseLIP-B TGIT being 93.9 in Table 13 versus 94.3 in Table 3, are drawbacks, but the stronger evidence for the central argument provides a substantial net improvement.
